claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can initially be retained in a metastable high-temperature BCC state.
Differential diffusion kinetics govern phase stability in the high-temperature BCC state of Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Al diffuses more slowly than the other constituents of Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
The slower intrinsic diffusion of Al creates local Al-enriched and Al-depleted regions in an otherwise uniform BCC matrix.
A critical local Al concentration threshold exists beyond which the uniform BCC state becomes thermodynamically unstable.
Crossing the local Al threshold triggers nucleation of secondary phases.
The secondary phases generated by this instability may include FCC phases or intermetallic compounds.
Isothermal annealing from 1100 °C to 1350 °C for 10, 30, and 60 minutes, coupled with Al tracer measurements, is the proposed intervention.
APT, SIMS, and tracer experiments will measure local Al fluctuations and Al diffusion profiles relative to the other constituents.
Longer annealing times at lower temperatures within the proposed range will produce greater local Al inhomogeneity.
Greater local Al inhomogeneity will correlate with the onset of FCC or intermetallic secondary-phase formation.
Rapid quenching from the high-temperature BCC state will preserve a compositionally homogeneous BCC baseline by preventing significant diffusion.
The proposed diffusion-controlled mechanism applies approximately between 1100 °C and 1350 °C.
Above the proposed temperature range, homogenization maintains a homogeneous alloy.
Below the proposed temperature range, the alloy will already have transformed completely.
Short-range atomic ordering is a plausible alternative to differential Al diffusion as the cause of phase transformation.
The mechanism would be falsified if Al does not diffuse at a significantly different rate from the other elements or if changing Al mobility does not alter the onset or extent of transformation.
